# @rxova/react-password-input

> A headless, accessible password input for React: a reveal toggle that keeps the
> caret, a Caps Lock warning read off the real modifier, a requirements checklist,
> and a strength meter that costs about 1 kB instead of the ~400 kB a wordlist
> estimator costs. Zero runtime dependencies. No stylesheet to import.

## Install

    npm install @rxova/react-password-input

`react >= 18` is the only peer dependency.

## Minimal working example

```tsx
import { PasswordInput } from '@rxova/react-password-input'

export function SignIn() {
  return <PasswordInput label="Password" name="password" autoComplete="current-password" />
}
```

On a sign-up or change-password form, set `autoComplete="new-password"` and opt
into the meter:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { PasswordInput, commonRules } from '@rxova/react-password-input'

export function SignUp({ email }: { email: string }) {
  const [valid, setValid] = useState(false)

  return (
    <>
      <PasswordInput
        label="Choose a password"
        name="password"
        autoComplete="new-password"
        showStrength
        minScore={3}
        minLength={10}
        userInputs={[email]}
        rules={[commonRules.digit, { ...commonRules.symbol, optional: true }]}
        onValidityChange={setValid}
      />
      <button type="submit" disabled={!valid}>
        Create account
      </button>
    </>
  )
}
```

`onChange` receives the **string**, not an event.

## Props

`<PasswordInput>` — the full surface is `PasswordInputProps` in the published types.

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | — | Controlled password. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | — | Uncontrolled initial password. Ignored when `value` is set. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Emits the string, not an event. |
| `revealed` | `boolean` | — | Controlled reveal state. Omit to let the component own it. |
| `defaultRevealed` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial reveal state when uncontrolled. |
| `onRevealChange` | `(revealed: boolean) => void` | — | |
| `hideRevealToggle` | `boolean` | `false` | Drops the reveal button entirely. |
| `hideOnBlur` | `boolean` | `true` | Re-masks when focus leaves the field. |
| `revealLabel` | `string \| ((state: PasswordRevealState) => string)` | `'Show password'` / `'Hide password'` | Accessible name for the toggle. |
| `revealIcon` | `ReactNode \| ((state: PasswordRevealState) => ReactNode)` | a built-in eye glyph | |
| `showStrength` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders the strength meter. |
| `estimate` | `(password: string) => PasswordStrength` | the built-in `estimateStrength` | Swap in a zxcvbn adapter if you want wordlists. |
| `blocklist` | `string[]` | — | Extra low-entropy strings to penalise, e.g. your product name. |
| `userInputs` | `string[]` | — | Email/username/name the user typed elsewhere. Nothing leaves the browser. |
| `strengthLabel` | `(strength: PasswordStrength) => ReactNode` | `'Very weak'` … `'Strong'` | Caption under the meter. |
| `minScore` | `PasswordScore \| null` | `null` | Minimum 0–4 score to count as valid. `null` disables the gate. |
| `rules` | `PasswordRule[]` | one length rule | NIST SP 800-63B leads with length and advises against composition rules. |
| `showRules` | `boolean` | `true` when `rules` was provided | Renders the requirement checklist. |
| `minLength` | `number` | `8` | Drives the default rule and the native `minlength`. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | `128` | Native `maxlength`. Always applied; the prop only moves the cap. Double NIST's 64-character floor, so passphrases are not truncated. A value below `minLength` or non-finite falls back to the default. |
| `onValidityChange` | `(valid: boolean) => void` | — | Fires when "all required rules met and `minScore` reached" flips. |
| `capsLockWarning` | `boolean` | `true` | |
| `capsLockLabel` | `ReactNode` | `'Caps Lock is on'` | |
| `checkCompromised` | `(password: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<boolean>` | — | Your breach lookup. The library never makes a request itself. |
| `checkCompromisedDelay` | `number` | `400` | Debounce before `checkCompromised` runs, in ms. |
| `compromisedLabel` | `ReactNode` | a stock sentence | Shown when `checkCompromised` resolves true. |
| `name` | `string` | — | Posts natively in a `<form>`; the name RHF/Formik bind to. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `autoComplete` | `string` | `'current-password'` | Set `'new-password'` on sign-up and change-password forms. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | — | |
| `onBlur` | `(event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | — | Fires when focus leaves the whole control, not the input alone. |
| `onFocus` | `(event: FocusEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | — | |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Focuses the field on mount. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Accessible name when there is no `label`. Wins over `label`. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Sets `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid`. |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | — | ids of external error/help text; merged with the ids this component owns. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | — | Accessible name for the field. **Not rendered** — supply your own `<label htmlFor={id}>` for a visible one. |
| `id` | `string` | — | Base id; input, meter, checklist and warnings derive theirs from it. |
| `className` | `string` | — | |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | — | |
| `onWarn` | `(warning: PasswordWarning) => void` | `console.warn` | Development-only notice that a prop was coerced. Stripped from production builds. |

Also exported: `usePasswordInput` for your own markup — its result carries
`clear()` alongside `setValue`, matching every other hook in the suite — `estimateStrength` and
`STRENGTH_LABELS`, and the rule helpers `commonRules`, `defaultRules`,
`evaluateRules`, `rulesSatisfied`.

## Styling

There is no stylesheet. Set CSS custom properties on any ancestor:

`--rx-password-gap`, `--rx-password-field-gap`, `--rx-password-toggle-size`,
`--rx-password-meter-height`, `--rx-password-meter-gap`,
`--rx-password-meter-radius`, `--rx-password-meter-track`,
`--rx-password-meter-fill`, `--rx-password-meter-fill-1` …
`--rx-password-meter-fill-4`, `--rx-password-rules-indent`.

Keep `--rx-password-toggle-size` at `1.5rem` or above: at the default font size that is
the 24×24 CSS pixels WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) requires.

Or target the `data-*` attributes, which are public API covered by semver:
`data-rx-password-root`, `data-rx-password-field`, `data-rx-password-input`,
`data-rx-password-toggle`, `data-rx-password-caps-lock`, `data-rx-password-meter`,
`data-rx-password-segment`, `data-rx-password-strength`,
`data-rx-password-strength-label`, `data-rx-password-rules`,
`data-rx-password-rule-marker`, `data-rx-password-compromised`,
`data-rx-password-announcement`, plus the state hooks `data-revealed`,
`data-valid`, `data-score`, `data-filled`, `data-met`, `data-rule`,
`data-disabled`, `data-invalid`.

## Three mistakes to avoid

1. **Treating the score as a security guarantee.** `estimateStrength` returns a
   0–4 bucket and an entropy estimate *after* penalties — a comparator for
   nudging a user, not a measurement of offline-attack cost. Server-side policy
   still belongs on the server.
2. **Leaving `autoComplete` at its default on a sign-up form.** The default is
   `'current-password'`, which is right for sign-in and wrong everywhere else:
   password managers offer to fill instead of offering to generate.
3. **Expecting `checkCompromised` to make a request.** It never does. You supply
   the lookup — wire it to a k-anonymity endpoint so the plaintext stays local —
   and it is called debounced with an `AbortSignal` that fires when the password
   changes again or the component unmounts.
